source_text: Διὸ δεῖ πάντως σε τὸν σοβαρὸν καὶ δυνατὸν καὶ πλούσιον ἐπιστήσασθαι ἑαυτῷ τινα ἄνθρωπον θεοῦ καθάπερ ἀλείπτην καὶ κυβερνήτην. αἰδοῦ κἂν ἕνα, φοβοῦ κἂν ἕνα, μελέτησον ἀκούειν κἂν ἑνὸς παρρησιαζομένου καὶ στύφοντος ἅμα καὶ θεραπεύοντος. οὐδὲ γὰρ τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς συμφέρει τὸν ἀεὶ χρόνον ἀκολάστοις μένειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ δακρῦσαι καὶ δηχθῆναί ποτε ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑγείας τῆς πλείονος. οὕτω καὶ ψυχῇ διηνεκοῦς ἡδονῆς οὐδὲν ὀλεθριώτερον· ἀποτυφλοῦται γὰρ ἀπὸ τῆς τήξεως, ἐὰν ἀκίνητος τῷ παρρησιαζομένῳ διαμείνῃ λόγῳ. τοῦτον καὶ ὀργισθέντα φοβήθητι, καὶ στενάξαντα † λυπήθητι, καὶ ὀργὴν παύοντα αἰδέσθητι, καὶ κόλασιν παραιτούμενον φθάσον. οὗτος ὑπὲρ σοῦ πολλὰς νύκτας ἀγρυπνησάτω, πρεσβεύων ὑπὲρ σοῦ πρὸς θεὸν καὶ λιτανείαις συνήθεσι μαγεύων τὸν πατέρα· οὐ γὰρ ἀντέχει τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτοῦ τὰ σπλάγχνα δεομένοις. δεήσεται δὲ καθαρῶς ὑπὸ σοῦ προτιμώμενος ὡς ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μηδὲν ὑπὸ σοῦ λυπούμενος, ἀλλ᾿ ὑπὲρ σοῦ. τοῦτό ἐστι μετάνοια ἀνυπόκριτος. »θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται« οὐδὲ προσέχει κενοῖς ῥήμασι· μόνος γὰρ ἀνακρίνει μυελοὺς καὶ νεφροὺς καρδίας καὶ τῶν ἐν πυρὶ κατακούει καὶ τῶν ἐν κοιλίᾳ κήτους ἱκετευόντων ἐξακούει καὶ πᾶσιν ἐγγύς ἐστι τοῖς πιστεύουσι καὶ πόρρω τοῖς ἀθέοις, ἂν μὴ μετανοήσωσιν.
thought_title: The rich need a trainer of the soul
orientation: Clement is addressing the rich person directly, telling him to submit to a man of God as trainer and pilot, and to accept rebuke, because repentance must be sincere and God sees the heart.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore it is necessary [for] you, the haughty and powerful and rich [person], to set over yourself some man of God, just as a trainer and a pilot. Respect even one [person], fear even one [person], practice to hear even one [person] speaking boldly and stinging at the same time and healing. For neither is it beneficial for the eyes to remain always licentious, but also to weep and to be bitten at some time for the sake of the greater health. Thus also for the soul nothing is more destructive than continuous pleasure; for it is blinded from the melting, if it remains unmoved by the word spoken boldly. This [man] both when angry fear, and when groaning be grieved, and when stopping anger respect, and when asking off punishment anticipate. This [man] let him stay awake many nights on your behalf, interceding on your behalf to God and with customary supplications charming the Father; for his inward parts do not hold out against his children when they beg. And he will ask purely, being honored by you as an angel of God and being grieved in nothing by you, but on your behalf. This is unfeigned repentance. "God is not mocked," nor does he attend to empty words; for he alone examines marrows and kidneys of the heart and hears those in fire and hears out those in the belly of the sea-monster who supplicate and is near to all who believe and far from the godless, unless they repent.

choices.why: The athletic image of an anointing-coach fits Clement's agonistic language; 'trainer' is plain and literal.
The nautical image of a steersman guiding the soul; 'pilot' is the standard English for this metaphor.
The verb means to be astringent or biting; 'stinging' preserves the medicinal sharpness paired with healing.
The Greek word denotes the bowels as the seat of compassion; 'inward parts' is literal and avoids the modern anatomical narrowing of 'bowels.'
The verb means to enchant or bewitch; Clement uses it boldly of the intercessor's supplications moving the Father, so 'charming' keeps the striking force.
The standard biblical rendering of the Greek term for sincere, without hypocrisy; it preserves the negative prefix.

pass_b_english: So then, you who are proud and powerful and rich must by all means set over yourself some man of God, as a pilot and a steersman. Respect at least one person; fear at least one person; practice listening to at least one person who speaks boldly and stings and heals at the same time. For it is not good for the eyes to remain unrestrained forever; sometimes they must weep and be bitten for the sake of greater health. In the same way, nothing is more destructive to the soul than continuous pleasure, for it is blinded by its own wasting away if it remains unmoved by the word that speaks boldly. Fear this man when he is angry, be grieved when he groans, respect him when he puts a stop to anger, and get ahead of him when he pleads for punishment to be averted. Let him stay awake many nights on your behalf, interceding for you before God and charming the Father with his accustomed supplications, for he his heart cannot hold out against his children when they beg. He will pray purely if he is honored by you as an angel of God and is not grieved by you in anything, but only on your behalf. This is unfeigned repentance. God is not mocked, nor does he attend to empty words, for he alone examines the marrows and kidneys of the heart, and he hears those in the fire and listens to those begging in the belly of the sea-monster, and he is near to all who believe and far from the godless, unless they repent.
notes: The dagger before λυπήθητι marks a suspected textual corruption or uncertainty in the source; the gloss renders the transmitted word 'be grieved' as it stands.

problems.quote: Fear this man when he is angry, grieve when he groans, respect him when he puts a stop to anger, and spare him when he asks for punishment.
problems.source_quote: τοῦτον καὶ ὀργισθέντα φοβήθητι, καὶ στενάξαντα † λυπήθητι, καὶ ὀργὴν παύοντα αἰδέσθητι, καὶ κόλασιν παραιτούμενον φθάσον.
problems.why: The English reverses the attitudes: Greek says be sad, be ashamed, despise; English says grieve, respect, spare.
problems.fix: Fear him when he is angry, be sad when he is restrained, be ashamed when he ceases anger, and despise him when he asks for punishment.

problems.why: The quotation 'God is not mocked' with this exact wording appears in Galatians 6:7, but Clement's context and the surrounding material (examining hearts, hearing those in fire and fish belly) strongly echoes Psalm 7:9-10 LXX and especially the language of Jeremiah 11:20 / 17:10 / 20:12 about God testing kidneys and heart, plus Jonah. However, the exact phrase θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται is indeed Pauline (Gal 6:7). But Clement's combination with 'he alone examines marrows and kidneys of the heart' is from Jeremiah/Septuagint, not Galatians. The citation is misleading as a single reference; but more critically, the verse in Galatians 6:7 is about sowing and reaping, not about God examining hearts. The reference should likely be left unattributed or multiple, but Galatians 6:7 alone is wrong for the composite quotation.
problems.fix: God is not mocked, nor does he attend to empty words
problems.ruling: Parenthetical “Galatians 6:7” misattributes whole passage; phrase alone matches but citation misleads.

dismissed.why: "μαγεύων" here means working on/entreating by spells, not "charming" in the modern sense of delighting; the sense is magical compulsion or powerful entreaty, not pleasant charm.
dismissed.note: 'Charming' in the sense of casting a charm is a fair rendering of μαγεύων.
